newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dollar buoys German shares, mkt closes off highs.
newsitem.headline: Dollar buoys German shares, mkt closes off highs.

text.p: Germany shares hit a record close in bourse trade on Monday -- boosted by the dollar's ongoing resilience against comments aimed at braking its rise -- and ended later screen-based trade broadly higher.

The 30-share blue-chip DAX index crossed the 3,220-point hurdle early in bourse trade to hit an all-time intraday high of 3,228.58 points and later set a lifetime closing high of 3,216.14, up 0.9 percent.
In post-bourse trade, the IBIS DAX eased slightly to 3,211.01 points, as the rally's momentum faded.

The dollar was the focus of the day as it breached 1.69 marks in early dealings on a report, later denied by the Bundesbank, that German officials wanted the U.S. currency to trade between 1.70 marks and 1.75 marks.
While the dollar lost ground on the Bundesbank denial, it still managed to hold above 1.68 marks -- seen as a positive signal for German exporters.
"The market is really rising off the dollar's strength," said one trader.
Export-oriented shares, particularly chemicals and automaker BMW which rose 36 marks to 1,159 marks in bourse trade, all benefited from the stronger dollar, dealers said.

The chemical sector, long favoured on the German bourse, saw further gains over the session. Bayer AG ended up 1.56 marks at 67.98 marks, Hoechst AG ended up 85 pfennigs at 75.60 marks and BASF ended up 31 pfennigs at 63.35 marks.

German banks were also in favour over the course of floor trade but underperformed relative to exporters. Commerzbank AG ended up 20 pfennigs at 43.50 marks, Deutsche Bank AG ended 38 pfennigs higher at 84.48 marks.
Dresdner Bank AG ended floor trade off earlier highs at 53.40 marks, up seven pfennigs, amid some profit-taking.
